request.prompt:
Project: expressjs__express
Below are verified claims extracted from the sources. Write up to 8 overview claims that explain how the parts fit together (architecture, main flows, cross-cutting rules). Each overview claim must list the ids of the claims that support it.

Return: {"overview":[{"text":"one sentence, max 40 words","supports":["c3","c17"]}]}

c1 [Readme.md] Express requires Node.js version 18 or higher before installation.
c2 [Readme.md] Express supports over 14 template engines via @ladjs/consolidate.
c3 [Readme.md] The generator executable express-generator's major version is specified to match Express's version.
c4 [Readme.md] The test suite for Express is executed using the command npm test.
c5 [Readme.md] The original author of the Express framework is TJ Holowaychuk.
c6 [Readme.md] Express is licensed under the MIT license.
c7 [index.js] The entry point file index.js re-exports the module located at ./lib/express.
c8 [lib/application.js] app.use flattens arguments, accepts path prefixes, and for mounted apps it wraps them to restore original request and response prototypes before invoking next.
c9 [lib/application.js] Modifying settings via app.set dynamically compiles and sets corresponding functions for 'etag', 'query parser', and 'trust proxy'.
c10 [lib/application.js] app.get acts as a configuration getter when called with a single argument, rather than declaring an HTTP GET route handler.
c11 [lib/application.js] app.listen creates an HTTP server with the app as handler and starts listening with the provided arguments.
c12 [lib/application.js] If a callback is passed to app.listen, it is wrapped with once and attached as an error event listener on the server.
c13 [lib/application.js] The logerror helper outputs an error via console.error unless the app's env setting equals 'test'.
c14 [lib/application.js] The tryRender helper invokes view.render and catches any synchronous error to pass it to the callback.
c15 [lib/express.js] The main export of the express module is the createApplication function.
c16 [lib/express.js] createApplication creates a function app(req, res, next) that delegates handling to app.handle(req, res, next).
c17 [lib/express.js] createApplication mixes EventEmitter.prototype and the application prototype into app without overwriting existing descriptors.
c18 [lib/express.js] createApplication invokes app.init() before returning the created app instance.
c19 [lib/express.js] The module exports the application, request, and response prototypes.
c20 [lib/express.js] The module exposes Router and Route from the router dependency.
c21 [lib/express.js] The module exposes json, raw, text, and urlencoded from body-parser, and static from serve-static.
c22 [lib/request.js] The request object `req` inherits from `http.IncomingMessage.prototype` and is exported directly.
c23 [lib/request.js] `req.get` aliases `req.header` and treats 'referer' and 'referrer' interchangeably when looking up request headers.
c24 [lib/request.js] The `query` getter delegates parsing to the application's `'query parser fn'` setting, returning an empty null-prototype object if disabled.
c25 [lib/request.js] The `protocol` getter trusts `X-Forwarded-Proto` only when the app's `trust proxy fn` accepts `this.socket.remoteAddress` at index 0.
c26 [lib/request.js] `req.ips` uses `proxyaddr.all`, reverses the address list to order from farthest to closest proxy, and drops the socket remote address.
c27 [lib/request.js] The `hostname` getter parses `this.host` and accounts for IPv6 literal brackets before locating a port delimiter.
c28 [lib/response.js] res.status enforces that the status code is an integer between 100 and 999 inclusive, throwing TypeError or RangeError otherwise.
c29 [lib/response.js] res.send automatically routes non-null, non-ArrayBuffer-view objects, numbers, and booleans to res.json.
c30 [lib/response.js] res.sendFile requires the path to be absolute unless a root option is explicitly specified.
c31 [lib/response.js] Setting a Content-Type header with an Array value throws a TypeError.
c32 [lib/response.js] Setting a signed cookie requires req.secret to be configured, otherwise res.cookie throws an Error.
c33 [lib/response.js] res.redirect encodes the destination URL, supports content negotiation for text and HTML, and ends with an empty body on HEAD requests.
c34 [lib/response.js] The internal stringify function escapes HTML-sensitive characters '<', '>', and '&' to unicode escape sequences when the escape flag is enabled.
c35 [lib/utils.js] exports.methods provides an array of lowercased HTTP method names supported by Node.js.
c36 [lib/utils.js] exports.compileETag maps true and 'weak' to exports.wetag, 'strong' to exports.etag, false to undefined, and throws TypeError for unrecognized values.
c37 [lib/utils.js] exports.compileQueryParser configures query parsing using querystring.parse for true/'simple', qs.parse with allowPrototypes: true for 'extended', and throws TypeError on unknown values.
c38 [lib/utils.js] exports.normalizeType parses MIME types containing '/' with acceptParams, or resolves extensions via mime.lookup, falling back to 'application/octet-stream'.
c39 [lib/view.js] View constructor throws an error if neither the provided view name has a file extension nor defaultEngine is provided in options.
c40 [lib/view.js] The tryStat helper calls fs.statSync and catches any thrown exception, returning undefined instead of rethrowing.
